entries.name: audio-check

entries.name: audit-scene
entries.description: re-read audit of a saved scene (B-1511): recounts triangles, textures (count and dimensions), placed instances and collision from the artifact itself -- never from the generator -- and compares them with the generation spec set (B-1509; default: the spec_set folder next to the scene). Differences come back per check with the expected and recounted values; families the artifact cannot express are reported not_countable with the reason

entries.name: autopilot
entries.description: replay a saved operation sequence (uzu-autopilot/1, B-312) specification image registry (B-1222, see ai_loop/spec_registry.py): registers specification illustrations (--id ID --image PATH), binds scenes (--scene res://... observed/inferred element correspondences (illustration regions <-> scene nodes)
entries.usage: uzu.py autopilot <project> <sequence.json> [--seed N] [--state a,b] [--log l.jsonl] --image-id ID [--report report.json --spec spec.json]), and maintains shared

entries.name: building
entries.description: procedural buildings (B-1219): houses and shops from parameters (width, depth, floors, roof, wall, seed) with real openings, frames and eaves in geometry, a high-density version baked down to a practical GLB with a PBR texture set; prints per-building triangle counts, the bake miss rate and GLB paths, and renders the street three ways (WorldGen-style, grey recipe, textured recipe)
entries.fallback: Without Blender, place a ready-made GLB, or build the building inside the engine instead (uzu.py build from a JSON spec, or UZUWorldGen's built-in houses).

entries.name: caps
entries.description: the agent capability profile (B-404): the capabilities this agent declares (image_gen, gpu, blender, browser), from --caps, $UZU_AGENT_CAPS and/or a JSON profile file ($UZU_AGENT_PROFILE); tools adapt to it

entries.name: catalog
entries.description: search the feature catalog (B-403): every command, MCP tool, preset, tool script and UZU class, generated from their definitions by ai_loop/make_catalog.py into ai_loop/catalog.json; use it to discover what exists before reading the docs. With a capability profile (B-404), matches are annotated with missing_capabilities

entries.name: collision-check
entries.description: mechanical collision check of a saved scene (B-1224): rasterizes the collision and the visuals onto a grid and checks them geometrically -- visual footprints collision does not cover, collision no visual explains, wall leaks (visual barrier, collision gap) and plugged gaps, walkable connectivity from the starts under the step rule (unreachable places, disconnected starts with the bottleneck and its required rise, pockets), and overlapping collision of different bodies. Findings carry coordinates; --heatmap writes a top-down PNG of the same raster. Static and geometric; the dynamic proof is the physics walker (map walk-graph)
entries.usage: uzu.py collision-check <project> --scene res://x.tscn [--start x,z ...] [--cell 0.5] [--step 0.25] [--char-width 0.7] [--body-height 1.8] [--out report.json] [--heatmap map.png]

entries.name: feel-report
entries.description: feel proxy metrics (B-1112, see ai_loop/feel_report.py and ai_loop/selfplay/feel_probe.gd): a self-verifying play sampled per frame -- per game event, the input -> reaction latency, hitstop / slowmo segments, shake and kick curves, flash segments and UI easing samples. Numbers for comparing runs (juice on/off, presets), never a "feels good" verdict; --no-juice measures the same play with the game's juice calls disabled, --probe-selftest fires one effect per channel without gameplay

entries.name: font-locale-check
entries.description: font locale check (B-1316, see ai_loop/font_locale_check.py): the ink top of 、 (U+3001) and 。 (U+3002) must sit in the lower half of the body band measured from the same font's kana/kanji -- JP faces pass (top at 0.33..0.36 of the band), centred TC/HK faces fail (0.65..0.67). The face of a TTC is chosen with the face flag; list-faces prints the face names. Needs fontTools. Exit 0 = pass, 1 = fail, 2 = usage/input error

entries.name: image-scene
entries.description: image-first scaffold (B-1221, see ai_loop/image_scene.py): the illustration becomes a B-1207 spec -- backdrop card, cut-out layer cards, candidate interact markers, the reference camera -- plus a generation report; the spec is built and a capsule walker walks its waypoints
entries.usage: uzu.py image-scene <project> --image illustration.png [--depth depth.png] [--out image_scene] [--registry spec_registry.json] [--image-id ID] [--scene res://x.tscn] [--fov 50] [--backdrop-width 26] [--no-build] [--no-walk] [--shot out.png] [--seconds 60]

entries.name: map
entries.description: a natural map or a city from a short spec (UZUWorldGen); every key is optional (presets); --spec-set also writes the generation spec set (B-1509) every map key with its default, range and meaning, and the presets a walker under physics walks the city's navigation mesh to each place; per-target result region-graph verification (B-1510): a walker under physics walks every edge of a B-1509 region graph in both directions; per-edge pass/fail JSON with frames, seconds and stuck points; --block-node fences one node in to prove that exactly its edges fail
entries.usage: uzu.py map <project> nature|city --scene res://main.tscn [--spec JSON-or-file] [--set key=value ...] [--overview top.png] [--replace] [--camera] [--look golden_hour] [--shot out.png] [--inline] [--spec-set [dir]] options [nature|city] <project> walk --scene res://x.tscn [--from spawn] [--to plaza,gate_east] [--seconds 90] <project> walk-graph --graph region_graph.json [--scene res://x.tscn] [--seconds 0] [--block-node <id>] [--out report.json]

entries.name: spec-diff
entries.description: spec-image diff verification (B-1223, see ai_loop/spec_diff.py): shoots the scene from its reference camera (or reuses --shot-png) and diffs the frame against the specification illustration -- composition (edge agreement), colour (histogram distance) and per-element presence from the B-1221 report or B-1222 registry -- as one pass/fail JSON with every measured number
entries.usage: uzu.py spec-diff <project> [--spec-image illustration.png] [--report report.json] [--registry spec_registry.json] [--scene res://x.tscn] [--shot-png shot.png] [--thresholds t.json] [--frames 8] [--out verdict.json]

entries.name: texture-route

entries.fallback: Without image_gen, texture-route picks the procedural PBR presets (B-1209) instead of a generated image (B-902).
entries.usage: uzu.py texture-route [--caps image_gen] [--profile caps.json] [--image generated.png] [--preset wood]

entries.name: ui

entries.usage: uzu.py ui <project> --spec ui.json [--shot out.png [--over res://game.tscn]] [--theme wafu|sf|fantasy] [--world fantasy|wafu|sf|horror|persona|pixel] [--font-subset]

entries.name: ui-quality
entries.description: AAA UI quality gate (B-1310, see ai_loop/ui_quality.py): texture repetition index (autocorrelation peak at tile lags), WCAG contrast (body >= 4.5, heading >= 3.0, slider groove/fill >= 2.0), 5-state completeness (focus must not be StyleBoxEmpty), theme coverage of the standard controls and spacing/radius/shadow scale conformance, as one uzu-ui-quality/1 JSON verdict. With --texture-image (an empty-panel sheet at native resolution) the texture is also scored on its own: designed micro-patterns by period residue + cell uniformity, other materials by a visibility index, plus frame centre-slice coverage. Theme data comes from --probe or from running ai_loop/ui_quality_probe.gd with --engine. Exit 0 = pass, 1 = fail
entries.usage: uzu.py ui-quality [--probe probe.json] [--engine PATH] [--theme wafu] [--image shot.png] [--region x,y,w,h] [--texture-image sheet.png] [--texture-region x,y,w,h] [--out report.json]

The result names places to use next (spawn, peak, lake, clearings) with positions, and counts. Same spec, same map. A wrong key comes back with the closest valid one; call map_options for every key.

Every finding carries coordinates and a severity; ok when no finding is an error. --heatmap also writes a top-down PNG of the raster. entries.description: List every key of map_nature and map_city with its default, what it accepts and what it does, and the presets.

entries.name: map_walk
entries.description: Self-verifying walk on a generated city: a walker under physics (capsule, gravity, collisions, curb steps) follows the navigation mesh from one place to each target in turn. Per target: reached or not, seconds, meters walked against the straight distance, and where it got stuck (position, what it hit). ok when every target was reached.

entries.name: map_walk_graph
entries.description: Region-graph walking verification (B-1510): a walker under physics (capsule, gravity, collisions, curb steps) walks every edge of a B-1509 region graph (uzu-region-graph/1) in both directions — along the navigation mesh where it is on it, steering straight at the target where there is none — and returns per-edge pass/fail with frames, seconds, meters walked and stuck points. ok when every edge passed both ways. block-node fences one node in with walls, to prove exactly its edges fail. The scene must already contain the generated map the graph describes.

entries.name: node_add
entries.description: Add a node of a class under a parent and save; 'set' is a JSON object of initial property values.

entries.name: node_call
entries.description: Call a method on a node and return the result; 'args' is an array in Godot text format.

entries.name: node_get
entries.description: Read a node property (supports indexed paths like position:y).

entries.name: node_instance
entries.description: Instance another scene under a parent and save.

entries.name: node_props
entries.description: List a node's inspector properties and their values.

entries.name: node_remove
entries.description: Remove a node (not the root) and save.

entries.name: node_reparent
entries.description: Move a node under another parent and save.

entries.name: node_set
entries.description: Set a node property and save. Values use Godot text format: 1.5, "text", Vector3(1, 2, 3); res:// paths load resources; resource class names (BoxMesh) create one.

entries.name: panorama
entries.description: Capture a 360-degree equirectangular panorama around the main camera and save a PNG.

entries.name: pbr_presets_apply
entries.description: Give bare models procedural PBR materials (wood, stone, brick, dirt, grass, plaster, tile: seamless textures made here, then albedo/normal/ORM), triplanar and tinted by each model's own color; untextured models look cheap.

entries.name: project_export
entries.description: Export the project with a preset; lists the files written.

entries.name: project_map
entries.description: A static map of the project for understanding it: files by kind, dependencies both ways (incl. preload/extends), scenes with nodes, scripts, instanced scenes and signal connections, autoloads, global classes.

entries.name: project_run
entries.description: Run the project headless for some frames; returns errors and the log tail.

entries.name: project_uids
entries.description: Check UIDs against the files: duplicates, missing or orphan .uid files, references whose UID is stale or whose path moved; each with a proposed fix. 'fix' applies them.

entries.name: project_validate
entries.description: Load every scene, resource and script of the project; list problems (missing files, broken scripts with errors, missing main scene or autoloads).

entries.name: replay_compare
entries.description: Compare replay JSON or JSONL and report the first differing field. Snapshots matches expected fields at each frame or time.

entries.name: resource_get
entries.description: Read a property of a resource file.

entries.name: resource_new
entries.description: Create a resource file (.tres) of a class, with optional initial values.

entries.name: resource_props
entries.description: List a resource file's inspector properties and values.

entries.name: resource_set
entries.description: Set a property of a resource file and save.

entries.name: scatter
entries.description: Spread props (stones, tufts, flowers) over a surface node as one MultiMesh and save: even by area, the same layout for the same seed, filtered by slope, exclusion zones and spacing. Returns how many, where (bounds) and why some were rejected.

entries.name: scene_audit
entries.description: Re-read audit of a saved scene (BACKLOG B-1511): re-opens the saved .tscn through the resource loader and recounts what is actually in the artifact -- mesh triangles, textures (count and dimensions), placed instances, collision shapes and bodies, lights, navigation meshes -- then compares the recount with the generation spec set (B-1509: asset_registry / scene_spec), never with the generator's own claims. Per check: match, difference (expected and recounted values) or not_countable with the reason. Also reports MultiMesh instances that are stored in the file but dropped on load. spec-set defaults to the spec_set folder next to the scene.

entries.name: scene_build
entries.description: Build a whole scene from one JSON spec (ground, models, scattered props, look, camera, lamps, particles, water, god rays) and get its richness report back; see ai_loop/look_samples/specs/village.json for an example and ai_loop/build_tool.gd for every key. Mistakes in the spec come back as a list of problems that name where they are.

entries.name: scene_enrich
entries.description: Make an existing scene richer in one call with a preset (village_rich, meadow, ruins: grass, flowers, stones, dust and a matching look; props keep off existing objects and stay near the camera on huge grounds). Returns the richness report before and after and the difference; applying again replaces the earlier props.

entries.name: scene_new
entries.description: Create a new scene file with a root node.

entries.name: scene_tree
entries.description: List the nodes of a scene with their types and scripts.

entries.name: screenshot
entries.description: Render the main scene without a GPU and save a PNG.

entries.name: script_attach
entries.description: Attach a script to a node and save.

entries.name: script_check
entries.description: Check a GDScript, .gdshader or .gdshaderinc file without a renderer; returns errors and warnings with file, line, column, code and message.

entries.name: setting_get
entries.description: Read a project setting.

entries.name: setting_set
entries.description: Change a project setting and save project.godot.

entries.name: sfx_generate
entries.description: Search, render, and place Lumina SFX WAV files into the Godot project from a uzu-sfx-request/1 JSON file.

entries.name: sfx_make
entries.description: Synthesize a sound effect (no sound files needed) and save it as a WAV: a preset (hit, jump, pickup, coin, explosion, laser, powerup, blip, land), varied by seed, with parameters changed by set. Returns its length, peak, loudness and pitch at the start and end, so you can judge it without listening.

entries.name: sfx_presets
entries.description: List the sound effect presets with their parameters, and every parameter with its default.

entries.name: sfx_sprite
entries.description: Pack several preset sound effects into ONE audio sprite WAV plus a JSON manifest of segments (name -> start/length in samples and seconds), so a game ships and loads one audio file instead of many. Play one segment in code with UZUSfx.play_sprite(parent, sprite, manifest, name). Returns the manifest, the totals and a description of the packed sound.

entries.name: signal_connect
entries.description: Connect a signal to a method persistently and save.

entries.name: ui_build
entries.description: Build a UI screen (HUD, dialogs, menus) from one JSON spec: a Control tree with anchors, containers and a theme (rounded panels, borders, shadows, buttons, bars), and optionally render it over a game scene. See ai_loop/look_samples/specs/hud.json for an example and ai_loop/ui_tool.gd for every key; mistakes come back as a list that names where they are.

entries.name: ui_report
entries.description: UI richness report of a UI scene (headless): how many controls, panels, buttons and texts, the smallest font, the depth, screen coverage and edge inset, and the problems with a fix for each (small text, text overflow, buttons too small for touch, no margin at the screen edge, overlapping panels, off screen, unstyled default look). ok is false when there are problems.

entries.name: vfx_describe
entries.description: Validate and normalize a visual-effect recipe (BACKLOG B-1109): parts (sparks, smoke, debris, ring, beam, light, shake, hitstop, kick, sfx) with every parameter filled in, out-of-range values clamped (listed as warnings), unknown parts rejected, and the total duration. Give a built-in name (explosion, laser) or a full recipe JSON. Fire a recipe in code with UZUVfx.fire / fire_named.

entries.name: vfx_recipes
entries.description: List the built-in visual-effect recipes (explosion, laser), each validated and normalized: their parts, parameters and total durations.

entries.name: biome_desert
entries.description: A desert biome as pure data (B-1219 stage 2): a UZUWorldGen nature spec in a file -- dry plains, no water, no trees, no snow, more rocks, sand-coloured ground. Feed it as-is: uzu.py map <project> nature --spec ai_loop/presets/map/biome_desert.json (keys starting with _ are metadata and are dropped by the map tool). Regional difference lives in data like this, never in generator code.
